chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had not performed the Aqeeqa for his child until he grew up, and was a youthful boy, or a man who had matured. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When a sacrifice is offered on his behalf, or the boy offers a sacrifice for himself, then his Aqeeqa has sufficed for him.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The newborn is held in pledge by his Aqeeqa; his parents either free him (from the pledge) or leave him (in it).'

key_terms.عَقِيقَتُهُ: Aqeeqa (ritual sacrifice offered for a newborn)
key_terms.فَكَّهُ: He freed him / discharged the pledge

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if Aqeeqa is not performed at birth and the child grows up?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the Aqeeqa obligation is not strictly time-bound, allowing for deferred fulfillment either by parents or the mature child, reflecting the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding ritual debts. It reinforces the Prophetic tradition of the newborn being 'pledged' (murtaḥan) by the sacrifice, a concept linking physical redemption to spiritual protection, often discussed in the context of removing minor sins or misfortune.
